speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We have decided to avail some of the Government’s expertise to the private sector, to level the playing field between the defenders and the attackers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: CII owners may need to incur cost to integrate these tools into their systems.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Even with these measures in place, we must be prepared that some threats will go undetected.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This is why defenders must remain vigilant and constantly enhance their capabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This brings me to my next point on innovation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: As pointed out by Mr Sharael Taha, autonomous AI agents are emerging threats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We must similarly harness technology to defend our critical systems.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: CSA will partner with CII owners to test the use of technologies, such as AI, to help enhance their efficiency and effectiveness of their cybersecurity operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We will share more details in due course.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The defenders will also need to be competent in using these tools effectively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Therefore, CSA will work with training providers to design and curate courses that equip cybersecurity professionals with specialised knowledge and skills on how to deal with APT threats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The responsibility of securing our CII systems cannot just rest on the shoulders of our frontline cyber defenders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The Board and management of CII owners must also do their part.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We will equip them with the relevant knowledge.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Since 2021, CSA has partnered the Singapore Management University to conduct the Cybersecurity Strategic Leadership Programme for C-suite leaders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The programme has trained 74 senior leaders thus far, such as Ms Dewi Anggraini from SMRT, Mr Andre Shori from Schneider Electric and Mr Kang Seng Wei from DBS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We intend to welcome the next batch of cybersecurity leaders by the second half of this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Just last year, Members may have seen articles stating that attackers gained unauthorised access to thousands of Internet of Things (IoT) devices, including routers, around the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Last year, attackers infected over 2,700 devices, such as baby monitors and routers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: When such personal devices are hacked, citizens' privacy can be compromised and their daily activities being disrupted.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: These devices can also be used unknowingly to launch attacks against others.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The Government will do more to protect our citizens against these malicious actors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: First, we will do more to ensure that the digital products that are sold in Singapore have baseline security safeguards in place.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This will make these products harder to be compromised.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Today, we require home routers to meet minimum cybersecurity requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This is because they are the gateways to networks and transmit sensitive information.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: They are currently required to meet Cyber Labelling Scheme, or CLS Level 1.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: CLS is like the energy efficiency tick label you see on household appliances, but instead of showing energy use, it tells you how cybersecure the device is.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: CLS ranges from Level 1 to Level 4, with Level 1 being the most basic standard.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We have seen threat actors using more advanced techniques to exploit home routers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Besides routers, IP cameras are another common target for cyber threat actors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Threat actors exploit these cameras to spy on individuals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Exploited images are even uploaded onto pornographic websites or used to blackmail individuals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: CSA will continue to monitor and review if more digital devices should be required to meet minimum cybersecurity standards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Second, for organisations which handle sensitive data, including personally identifiable information, we are considering to introduce more stringent cybersecurity and data protection obligations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The Government will take the lead in this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: CSA will also require the following three groups of entities who are operating, assessing or handling sensitive systems and data to meet Cyber Trust Mark Requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: These are the CII owners, auditors conducting cybersecurity audits on CII systems and CSA's licensed Cybersecurity Service Providers providing penetration testing and managed security operations centre services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Consultations with relevant stakeholders are ongoing and these measures will be implemented progressively over the next two years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We are also looking ahead to prepare for tomorrow's threats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Mr Kenneth Tiong sought to clarify Singapore's approach to quantum-safe migration.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We have been monitoring this technological trend closely.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We also take the position that PQC will be the mainstream solution for quantum-safe migration.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Singapore will take reference from the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) standard as the baseline.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: As Mr Tiong pointed out, this is the position taken by many other countries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: It is more for niche application, like securing high assurance communications.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Singapore takes a risk-oriented approach when it comes to quantum-safe migration.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The Government is reviewing the practical steps we can take for quantum-safe migration, including adoption of PQC and the appropriate role of QKD, if needed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We have started investing in capabilities to support businesses in quantum-safe migration.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In October 2025, CSA released a Quantum-Safe Handbook and Quantum Readiness Index to raise awareness of the associated risks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This provides additional options for businesses to integrate quantum-safe solutions, such as PQC and QKD, into their networks and systems.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: By supporting the provision of NQSN+ infrastructure and services, we aim to reduce the technical and financial barriers for organisations looking to implement quantum-safe solutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We are closely monitoring developments and will release guidance on this in due course.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We are prepared to adopt different technological solutions if they prove to be effective and able to meet our needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: MDDI is committed to improve the resilience and security of our digital infrastructure.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Mr Chairman, in today's world, many businesses provide seamless, effective and reliable digital services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: While we have made good progress, we can do better.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: We must acknowledge that citizens still encounter services that are slower than they should be, forms that ask for information we already have or systems that do not speak easily to one another.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: There are a few things that we can learn from LEGO sets.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: First, they are based on a strong understanding of their customers and how preferences change over time.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Every brick is designed to connect seamlessly with one another.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Builders do not need to reinvent the basic structure each time.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Third, customers can choose how simple or complex a model to build.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: For some, a simple LEGO DUPLO or LEGO City set is sufficient.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: And for others who want complexity, LEGO Technic or LEGO Education SPIKE sets offer advanced mechanical components.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: The analogy may sound simple, but the engineering discipline behind it is not.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: What do these lessons look like for us, in the Public Service?

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: We must understand our citizens continuously, not episodically.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: A service that felt intuitive ten years ago may feel slow or fragmented today.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: We must design modular systems and digital components that work across agencies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: When systems connect seamlessly, citizens experience Government as a whole.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: And we must be able to provide services that meet complex needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Our advanced shared tools, such as AI platforms and coding assistants, support us in building specialised components at scale.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: But when complexity is needed, the capability must already be there.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: To do all of this well, some of our habits must change.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Sometimes, digital transformation becomes a collection of projects.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Transformation is not about the number of digital projects launched.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: It is whether citizens find it simpler, faster and clearer to deal with the Government.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: But doing nothing, while expectations move ahead of us, is a risk.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: We must learn to manage that risk, not eliminate experimentation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Through initiatives, like Open Government Products' (OGP's) Hack for Public Good, our officers work closely with users to understand and address real pain points.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: A team observed that medical social workers spent long hours writing case notes after emotionally difficult conversations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Their first instinct was to build an automated transcription and summary tool.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: But the tool did not fully address the users' needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Our social workers wanted greater control over how case notes were structured, so that important information can be retrieved easily.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: When the generated notes were not organised clearly, they rewrote them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: The team refined the tool into Scribe, an AI-powered tool that transcribes conversations and generates summaries according to the topics and writing style chosen by the user.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: That time is not just a data point.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: If LEGO connectors were redesigned every year, no one could build anything coherent.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: In Government, incompatible systems have the same effect.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Previously, agencies often built separate systems for different needs, believing that every need was unique.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: While well-intentioned, this led to duplication and integration challenges.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Citizens feel the fragmentation when information cannot be shared across systems.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: We must provide and use common digital components, like secure logins and payment processing, built on shared standards for security and resilience.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: They should reuse, recombine and focus on what makes their missions unique.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: When the Health Sciences Authority (HSA) stepped up vaping enforcement last year, they needed a new system for their operations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: HSA built on shared tools from GovTech and OGP, such as Ownself Gather, a case management system, and Plumber, which allows officers to automate manual tasks, like tracking repeat offences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: When we build faster, we enforce faster and citizens are better protected.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Some services need simple, reliable components and we must resist the temptation to over-engineer.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: But sometimes, we do need advanced tools that can help us build better services and do so more quickly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Mr Henry Kwek asked how GovTech is embracing AI-centric IT development and encouraging its vendors to adopt such practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: We are providing common tools, such as commercial AI coding assistants that support Government developers and vendors with tasks like code completion.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: We also have AI tools for GovTech officers to build and deploy functional prototypes without writing code.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: For both the Public Service and our contracted vendors, these tools are governed by standards for secure development, safe AI use and data protection.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Our shared tools also help agencies build more inclusive and user‑centric services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: As Mr Sharael Taha highlighted, essential Government services should be accessible by everyone, including persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: One of our most valuable shared tools is called Oobee.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: It proactively detects accessibility issues on Government websites and suggests fixes, like including descriptive text that can be read aloud by Assistive Technology for our visually impaired users.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: It has shown us how even with good intentions, we may have blind spots.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: The success of our services rests on a strong foundation of trust.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Singaporeans use our digital services because they trust that these are secure and that they are dealing with legitimate Government officials.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Government official impersonation scams are a serious threat because they attack that trust directly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: For citizens to easily identify and trust calls from the Government, OGP and IMDA are developing systems for agencies to make calls with numbers that start with a common prefix.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Later on, we will display a recognisable caller name.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Many scammers also use local SIM cards for illicit purposes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: The Government will also apply analytics to SIM card registration data, within strict legal safeguards, to proactively detect and disrupt potential scam activities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: These measures focus on identifying suspicious registration patterns.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Think about what it takes to go from building a beginner LEGO set, maybe a simple car, a few dozen pieces, designed for a young child, to a full LEGO Education SPIKE robot.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: It is a different level of skill, confidence and ambition.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Our public officers must grow with the challenge.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Many of our loyal and hardworking public officers have spent years building skills for their work.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: With the tools around them changing fast, this can feel exciting for some.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: For others, it feels unsettling, as if the expertise they have worked hard to develop might be overtaken before they can fully use it.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Our job is not just to offer comfort, but to build capability.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: To give them the confidence to use a new tool and think: I can work with this.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: And I can tell whether the output is good or not.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: We have already started digital training for our Cabinet Ministers and Senior Public Service Leaders, as Minister Chan Chun Sing mentioned earlier.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: When they understand the digital landscape, they can guide change confidently and ask their teams the right questions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: For our broader Public Service, the goal is to ensure that no public officer feels powerless in a digital world.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: The Institute will equip our public officers with Digital, Data, Design and AI skills.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: We will focus not just on technology but on designing solutions that are citizen-centred and secure.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: We also need to address the outdated systems that no longer support our needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: These are systems built early in our digitalisation journey, using technology that was prevalent at the time.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Today, these systems are inflexible, expensive and difficult to integrate.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: They slow down policy change and hinder our ability to share information for seamless services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Rebuilding our systems will take time, but we are committed to this effort, because this is foundational to our digital transformation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Every modernisation effort gives us a chance to rebuild and create faster, connected systems that can better support service delivery.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: I have described what we must do, to improve our Government digital services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: We must understand our citizens continuously, build in a modular way and develop capabilities for complexity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: We will upgrade the skills of our public officers and rebuild many of our outdated systems over time.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: If we do this well, our citizens will feel the difference.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Their experience with Government will feel simpler, clearer and more human, especially at moments when citizens have little bandwidth to deal with Government.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: In those precious early days, what you want most is time with your baby, not multiple forms to fill.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: We have therefore integrated services around this life moment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: The aim is simple: fewer steps, fewer repeats, more time for families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: With AI, we can go one step further, from services that respond, to services that guide.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Take the SupportGoWhere portal, which consolidates Government schemes across 31 agencies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Imagine trying to look for support from nearly 300 options, across different life stages and needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Our seniors and their caregivers told us that they felt overwhelmed: too much information, too many pathways.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: The Senior Support Recommender will ask them several questions and then uses AI to recommend them the most relevant schemes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: We are still refining it, but this is the direction that we want to go: a government that helps citizens find the information that they need, instead of making them hunt for it.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Delivering better services also means that our precious human Public Service officers can focus their time and their resources on supporting those who truly are not able to use technology.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: They can be served by our officers in a more timely manner.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Better services must also be faster, because delays are not just administrative in nature.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: As our population ages, demand for healthcare professionals will rise.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: For patients and families waiting for care, this can mean earlier treatment, earlier support and less anxiety.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: These examples are not exceptions to be admired.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Our transformation will not happen overnight, but that is the standard that we will hold ourselves to.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: Mr Chairman, building digital capability is not just about chasing technology.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: It is about raising our standard of service.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
text: That is the standard and it is our responsibility to meet it.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Chairman, while technology has made our lives easier and offers the promise of a better future, we must ensure our digital society remains safe and vibrant.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Government will continue to play a strong role in protecting those who are most vulnerable to online harms.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: At the same time, we must also empower citizens to build the skillsets and confidence to navigate and learn in today's digital world, especially with the advent of AI.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I will outline MDDI's efforts in these areas.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Many of us have heard stories, or perhaps even know someone who is a victim of online harms.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Some victims have experienced online stalking, while others have had their intimate photos abused.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Often, victims and their families deal with tremendous distress and helplessness.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This is why the Online Safety (Relief and Accountability) Bill, passed in Parliament last November, is so crucial.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Upon assessment of a victim's report, the OSC can issue directions to disable access to harmful online content or restrict the perpetrator's online account.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Even as we set up the OSC to provide an additional avenue of support, I know that many parents are naturally worried about their children's daily digital activities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Children are amongst the most active digital users, and many parents are stretched as they juggle monitoring their children's digital usage with other commitments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In MDDI's Digital Parenting Study in 2025, over half of respondents wanted more Government support, including stronger legislation, to help them manage their children's digital activities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Ms He Ting Ru asked about efforts to better protect children from the harms and risks associated with social media.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We have taken progressive regulatory measures to address the concerns of parents and the community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Over the past three years, we introduced two Codes of Practice for Online Safety.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Codes require designated social media services and app stores to minimise Singapore users', especially children's exposure to harmful content.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Codes also require designated social media services and designated app stores to submit annual online safety reports to IMDA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: IMDA is presently assessing the annual online safety reports submitted by the designates social media services in 2025.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: IMDA's overall report will be published alongside designated social media services reports when ready.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Today, we already do age assurance in the physical world, like how supermarkets or convenience stores check the ID of customers before selling age restricted products, such as alcohol or tobacco.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As new risks continue to emerge, online safety remains a constant challenge around the world.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Some overseas jurisdictions have announced or implemented social media bans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Singapore also wants to strengthen protection for our children online and we want to do it right and take a holistic approach.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This would better ensure that online services are age-appropriate for users, including children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Consultations with the designated social media services are ongoing, and more details will be announced later this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Government remains vigilant regarding online harms outside of app stores and social media services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Some parents have expressed concerns about harms that online video games bring, including exposure to inappropriate content, cyberbullying and screen addiction.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We recognise these concerns and are studying whether safeguards on online video games are needed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We are also mindful of other types of online services that may pose a threat to online safety.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As Ms He Ting Ru pointed out, one example is the misuse of AI to generate indecent content, such as sexual content and violent content, in real time and at scale.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Chatbots that are embedded in social media services present unique risks as users, including children, can access them more easily.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Ms He also raised a recent worrying trend of users using prompts on X's chatbot, Grok, to replace the clothes of adults and children with revealing attire, such as bikinis.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We note that X has taken some measures to address the matter globally.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will continue to monitor the issue closely and will work with X to enhance online safety for Singapore users on its platform.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will not hesitate to take designated social media services to task if they have failed to comply with the SMS code.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We are also studying whether safeguards for AI chatbots are needed to better protect users from the harms caused by their misuse.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: While parents can look forward to stronger guardrails to protect our children from online harms, parents also play an important role in inculcating healthy digital habits in children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Parenting in the digital age is undoubtedly challenging.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We frequently hear stories of children being glued to their devices during family dinners, or parents feeling shut out from their children's digital spaces.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Some have even described parenting today as swimming against a relentless digital tide, while struggling to stay afloat amidst competing priorities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These concerns are real, and we want parents to know that they are not alone.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To address these concerns, MDDI has rolled out resources for parents and is strengthening efforts to make them more accessible in the community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Parents can access tips on how to guide their children's digital interactions on IMDA’s Digital for Life portal.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These are tailored to different digital milestones in the parenting journey, such as a child's first device use, first social media use and first online game.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Families with young children will also be supported by digital parenting workshops and webinars.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These sessions are designed to meet different needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Some support parents of younger children, while others engage families with youths who may encounter more challenging online situations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will continue to do more to support digital parenting and welcome suggestions on how we can improve our programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Preparing for the digital world requires us to not only be safe online users, but also purposeful and discerning learners.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We need to prepare our students and educators for an AI-enabled future, as Mr Henry Kwek and Ms Lee Hui Ying highlighted.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Educators play a critical role in the development of essential skills for our students.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Minister of State Jasmin Lau spoke earlier on enhancing public sector digital capabilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We are also doing more to grow educators' knowledge and understanding about technology.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I am glad that the feedback has been positive.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Many participants shared that the Smart Nation Educator Fellowship has sharpened their abilities to guide students to become thoughtful and responsible users of technology.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Ezal bin Sani, a Lead Teacher for History in Jurong Secondary School, was one of the Smart Nation Educator Fellowship fellows.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For a Secondary 1 History inquiry-based project on Singapore's migrant Chinese communities, Ezal’s students conducted AI-powered interviews with historical "coolies" and used ElevenLabs or Google NotebookLM to create their own AI podcasts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Initiatives like this demonstrate how powerful educational technology can be in our classrooms, with students critically assessing the information gleaned from AI tools to enhance their learning process.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This year, we are refining the fellowship to focus on the power and possibilities of AI.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Through workshops and industry visits, educators will better appreciate how AI is relevant in the workplace.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This can in turn support students' development of AI skills and competencies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will update programmes in our schools to meet emerging needs, just as we have done before.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As the Prime Minister shared, AI literacy is fundamental digital competency that will become even more important going forward.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Sharael Taha and Mr Darryl David asked about the Government's plans to make digital skills and tools available to every child, regardless of background.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will continue to ensure that AI literacy programmes remain accessible in our schools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Primary school students will learn the basics of AI, such as creating digital storybooks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Secondary school students will learn to use AI to create solutions for real-world problems.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As students experiment and learn with AI, they will also learn about the risks, limitations and responsible use.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Today, citizens can look to IMDA's Digital Skills for Life resources to pick up skills to navigate digital spaces.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This includes how to use Generative AI confidently and safely, as well as how to identify AI risks, such as misinformation, scams and deepfakes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Our libraries also provide important touchpoints for digital learning.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The National Library Board's (NLB's) S.U.R.E programme, which stands for Source, Understand, Research, Evaluate, encourages Singaporeans to evaluate the credibility and reliability of information.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: NLB will also offer roving experiential showcases across public libraries and other public spaces.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Members of the public can experience the uses and benefits of AI, and how to use GenAI safely and responsibly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will continue to provide targeted support for vulnerable groups.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: At SG Digital Community Hubs across Singapore, seniors can learn how to use digital services for daily tasks, such as booking medical appointments and mobile banking.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Citizens, particularly seniors, who need in-person support will still be able to receive assistance at Government agencies' physical service touchpoints and at ServiceSG Centres.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will also continue to collaborate with Digital for Life partners to help persons with disabilities participate meaningfully in our digital world.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For instance, Guide Dogs Singapore developed a toolkit to help members of the visually impaired community learn to use low vision accessibility features on the smartphone, such as the VoiceOver function.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Through these efforts, we are building an inclusive Singapore where every citizen can benefit from our digital future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Digital technologies, including AI, have become important ingredients in our daily lives and for the jobs of tomorrow.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Thus, it is important that all of us are equipped to not only have digital skills, but to use them confidently and thoughtfully.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Everyone is at a different stage of their digital journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Some are just starting to explore and experiment, while others are focused on enhancing their technical skills and putting them into practice.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This step-by-step approach allows us to engage different segments of our community and provide support that matches the level of their digital journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Staying true to our "gotong-royong" spirit, MENDAKI will bring together the whole community, including the M³ family, Malay/Muslim organisations, the MENDAKI Professional Networks, as well as partners from the public and private sectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: A good example is Mr Luqman-nul Hakim, who works as an AI engineer and has stepped forward to support Langkah Digital.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Luqman has led sessions on AI at Al Khair Mosque for over 30 participants and facilitated an AI workshop for more than 60 participants.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These programmes help cater to individuals with different abilities and interests in our community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Some introduce AI tools such as ChatGPT, while others focus on more advanced skills such as prompt engineering.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Digital champions, such as Luqman are the driving force behind Langkah Digital.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: They not only help to bring different groups together but also foster meaningful dialogue and collaboration around technology.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I hope that Langkah Digital will empower even more members in our community. : Mr Chairman, as technology keeps evolving, it is not enough for us to hone our technical skills.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To harness AI wisely, we need to ask the right questions and be discerning about the answers we get.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Therefore, our children need to develop capabilities to read and process information effectively from young.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I am spotlighting reading because it is a skill that is increasingly at risk in a world where information is delivered at break-neck speeds, often in short-form and visual formats.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: It improves our attention span, develops critical thinking skills, and builds creativity and empathy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: All these are essential qualities for us to use technology for the benefit of ourselves and others.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Promoting reading is therefore important in addressing the concerns raised by Members about social and intellectual degradation that might come with AI.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Ms Cassandra Lee asked how NLB is refreshing the libraries' role with families in mind.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We can start with encouraging parents to cultivate good reading habits in their children from a young age.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This also provides our children with a screen-free alternative in our device-heavy era.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This is why NLB will continue to partner with MOE to strengthen the library programme for schools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This includes an upcoming School Librarians of the Future Summit and webinars to empower student librarians as reading advocates and champions for information literacy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Student librarians can also broaden their learning, through volunteering, student attachments and learning journeys.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: NLB will do more to foster strong reading habits and plans will be shared in due course.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Our libraries also play a vital role in preserving and sharing our Singapore Stories.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These stories form the bedrock of our community and ensure that our collective experiences are not lost to time.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To mark Singapore's 60 years of Independence, NLB and MDDI launched a book and exhibition on The Albatross File, which documents the events, personalities and debates surrounding Singapore's journey to Independence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The exhibition has resonated strongly with the public.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To Mr Fadli Fawzi's observation that the exhibition departs from what he was taught in school, there has always been differing points of view on Singapore's separation from Malaysia.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This is unsurprising, given the nature of historical accounts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For example, British, Australian and New Zealand archives released from the early 1990s reflected the perspectives of their diplomats and governments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In 1998, full versions of the perspectives of Singapore's officials appeared.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Prof Albert Lau's "A Moment of Anguish" remains the most definitive account of the separation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The first volume of founding Prime Minister Mr Lee Kuan Yew's memoir also featured a gripping account.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As stated in the editorial notes of The Albatross File: Inside Separation, nothing material to the understanding of the separation was held back.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The documents published were reproduced in full, without redaction.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Members of the public, including Members of Parliament, can approach the National Archives of Singapore to look at all this declassified material and form their own nuanced views.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The experience of some countries with similar legislation shows that most, if not all, will still have carve-outs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Tony Blair's 2010 memoirs record his views on the UK's Freedom of Information Act, which was enacted while he was Prime Minister.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: He said, after leaving office, that "The Freedom of Information Act…is a dangerous Act   governments need to be able to debate, discuss and decide issues in confidence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Without the confidentiality, people are inhibited and the consideration of options is limited in a way that isn't conducive to good decision making.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Government has made more records available to the public over time and will continue to do so.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Singapore stories not only enhance our understanding of history but enable us to reimagine our future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I am glad to hear that it was well received, with most visitors giving it a rating of five out of five.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Experience was also an example of utilising digital innovations, such as AI and immersive storytelling, to present a multisensory experience.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: By pairing the experience with NLB's resources, visitors had the opportunity to learn more about using AI in their daily life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To conclude, Mr Chairman, as digital technologies become increasingly complex and sophisticated, their potential to transform our society and lives, whether for better or worse, has never been greater.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As the Malay peribahasa or proverb reminds us, "Berat sama dipikul, ringan sama dijinjing." We share responsibilities and work together to overcome challenges, be it big or small.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Harnessing technology for good as well as mitigating the negative impacts of technologies require more than just technical knowledge.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Ultimately, we need a whole-of-society effort that brings together the experiences and perspectives of the Government, industry, academia, civil society and citizens.

speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Let us work together to chart a bright and promising digital future for generations to come.

speaker: The Chairman
text: We have just around 25 minutes for clarifications.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I will prioritise Members who have filed cuts according to the amount of time they have filed.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: I believe the Minister did not get an opportunity to address my cut on the role of NAIC.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: My last supplementary question is on trust and regulatory credibility.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: Minister Josephine Teo shared that Singapore is known for our trust and regulatory credibility.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: Maybe that could be our differentiator and competitive advantage.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, it is just a little over two years since we formally started the process.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If I were to say up to now, what we are learning from it?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The first, perhaps to refer to the earlier handout that MTI distributed – this is on Kampong AI – as an example.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I recall that around 2023, we had visited a corner of San Francisco that was known as Cerebral Valley.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It was very captivating for us because the hacker houses had such an energy about them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Papers that were being published by universities in the morning, in the evening, they already have a talk and people would come in and say, this is how I am going to use it.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Then, a week later, a prototype would have already been built and venture capitalists were invited for show and tell.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: You could see that this generated a kind of buzz that was very enviable.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We really did not know how comprehensive our ecosystem was at the time, that would centre its attention on AI-related activities.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, we said, let us start with Lorong AI.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It was not called Lorong AI at the start.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We just decided that we just have to bring the community together.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We did not have our Cerebral Valley then.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We just had to see whether it could take off.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Because of that, we have the confidence to do Kampong AI.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But what is the reflection and what is the lesson learned there?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is that you can start small but dream big.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: You do not always have to have a Big Bang approach.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The second observation I would say is that in terms of how we have implemented ideas, actually, gaps are good opportunities.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: After we did Lorong AI, we were also building up AI Centres of Excellence.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If we did not have a good momentum with the AI Centres of Excellence, it will be hard to now try to push ahead with Champions of AI.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We do not have a base to begin with.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And one of those particular Centres of Excellence was in manufacturing.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: When we looked at the activities being carried out at that Centre of Excellence, we realised that there are common problems that a sectorial Centre of Excellence could do.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And then, it enabled us to think that perhaps in some sectors, there was a certain readiness for end-to-end transformation.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, the national AI Missions, in a way, grew out of that effort too.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Then, we asked ourselves, we now have activities in industry, we now have activities in Government, which Minister of State Jasmin Lau spoke about – AI activities.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In research, things were also happening in a very positive way.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: What that tells us is that research activities are picking up pace, because AI top talents are attracted by bold ambition and a willingness to tackle the big questions, the problems that confound many people.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The gaps, being opportunities specifically apply in the talent space.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We had started thinking broadly in terms of AI Creators.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That would be the people in Microsoft Research, Google DeepMind.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For example, in Google DeepMind, within the Singapore team, they are contributing to the development of the newest Gemini models.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, we had thought about AI Creators, we had thought about AI Practitioners – machine learning engineers, data scientists – and we had thought about users – the broad base.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As we were implementing the Centres of Excellence, we also realised that in between, you need people who both understand AI, not necessarily at the deepest level, but they have good domain expertise.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There is this idea that you need "bilingual" talent – people who know enough of AI, know enough of their domain and they can marry the knowledge together.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Even in terms of how we think about the AI talent spectrum, what originally was a gap now turns out to be an opportunity for us to do something about it.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The third relates specifically to your question about the role of NAIC.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We use it very much to talk about social solidarity.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It goes, "If you want to go fast, you go alone.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If you want to go far, you go together." It turns out that it applies to AI development too.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If we only confine ourselves to the effort that can be applied within the verticals – MDDI, you do this; MTI, you do this; I think we will remain effective in our own ways, but we will not get to synergise.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Lorong AI can become Kampong AI because there is JTC.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If JTC has not been seized with this idea, then this growth could not have quite come about.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, the NAIC is precisely to do these things.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Make the whole bigger than the sum of its parts.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It tends to be one-to-one, but what we need is many-to-many cooperation and we need the mechanism to sort things out – where to prioritise, where to apply more resources, where the exploration is heading into a dead end, what kinds of policy changes that you might need.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, the NAIC is not just an advisory role.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That is what it is intended to be.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Very quickly, Mr Chairman, I think there was also a question about trust and regulatory credibility, and whether we will set up institutions to do that.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: I think it is very important, so I do want to ask a little bit of clarification around that, more from an individual and citizen standpoint.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: How does this pan out and how can the ordinary citizen look forward to in terms of, what do they do with regards to the National AI Impact Programme and how do they access that?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: The other question I had was, related to this as well, in terms of digital literacy specific to AI.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: I did touch upon the point about life stages and whether in terms of the digital literacy, as we are looking at it for citizens, even for workers, how do we ensure that this is looked at from a life stage standpoint, rather than from an age or just a profile standpoint?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: And another question around responsible AI was that, given that it is widely used now and, in a lot of cases, for some very critical areas in terms of decision making, how do we ensure and how will the Government look at ensuring that biases are not kind of perpetuated?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: And the last point on inclusivity, given that AI is going to be very much part of our lives and it is not something we can ignore, how are we going to look at the multiple languages and supporting those in terms of people who are not so proficient in English?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For one, we will work very closely with trade associations and chambers as well as professional bodies for outreach.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There is very strong interest from these intermediaries to get the word out and we welcome their interest.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We already have existing programmes that serve as a useful base so, for example, the enterprise solutions will very largely be offered through the Productivity Solutions Grant scheme.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That will likely grow because of the interest and also because of the availability of the tools.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If we look at enterprises that already use some digital tools, the Member can imagine that the vendor goes to the enterprise and say, "If you add this AI tool on top of it, actually, you can do more things than you were able to previously." So, this is one way to propagate on a base that is already quite ready.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, through their own mechanisms, individuals can also be reached.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, those are the different ways in which we will propagate the access to the National AI Impact Programme.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If anyone comes to us and say, "This is what you can do." We are very keen to understand how.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I believe that our institutes of higher learning are also very much involved because they interact with the private sector and they have a lot of students who are interested to prototype solutions in order to implement them, so we will look at those as well.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Member's question about responsible AI biases, how to make sure they are not perpetuated.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The way we approach the potential risks and harms of AI is a multi-prong one.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In some instances, we already have safeguards that perhaps need to be sharpened.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, for example, pornography that could be enabled by AI, child sexual exploitation material.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: These are already prohibited under the Penal Code.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We can update the Penal Code to make it clear.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We can also think of instances, like the Workplace Fairness Act.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If there is a demonstration of bias in the recruitment process, then that piece of legislation can be relied upon, because it does not depend on how the unfairness, the discrimination was produced, so we can deal with it that way.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This was specifically to deal with AI-generated content that are applied to candidates in an election context, so we will continue to maintain this sort of nimble approach.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Use existing laws, sharpen the laws, if and when necessary, but also do not hesitate to introduce new measures when they are needed and when it is clear what can be done about them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, those are the things that we will do.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Inclusivity, I fully agree with you, multiple inclusivity.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I fully agree with you, multiple languages — perhaps I will ask Senior Minister of State Tan to reply because he has been working on this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: As we know, Singapore is a multilingual society and different communities take a lot of pride in their languages, especially mother tongues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: One part of the work is that MDDI looks at, specifically the "I" part of MDDI, is around information.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: There is a committee where we bring in academics, representatives from the media, the schools, around translation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: That is the National Translation Committee, which I help to oversee.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: One project that we are working on, as a very good example of how we are thinking about practical tools for AI, is about translation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: And translation is not just by using any tool, any large language models (LLMs), because you need local context, local nuances, for example, not everybody understands what "chope the table" is.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: So, how do you translate some of these local terms, especially local specific-context terms into different mother tongue languages?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Not just "copying and pasting" what other countries are doing, but fine-tuning, adapting, customising for our local context, and do so in a way that creates value and adds that element of inclusivity for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We hope to share more details later and hope to get the support of all Members.

speaker: The Chairman
text: We are fast approaching guillotine time, so I will take one more clarification.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Chairman, I would like to ask MDDI on what MDDI can do to set and communicate the right expectations for our people citizenry, given the fact that we are vastly transforming the way we interact with the citizens.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: I applaud the MDDI for the ambition and the determination to transform the way we do e-services.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Basically, in a nutshell, we are asking the Government to do more with less; do faster; do differently, not just transacting with Government, but also giving people advice, like SupportGoWhere.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: So, it is quite a big way of transformation of how we do things, in terms of Government service.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: And we are also, instead of developing services through coding, we are asking our civil service to orchestrate AI agents to code.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: With new ways of doing, there is always a risk of things not working out initially.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: So, how are we going to set the right expectations?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Like I think Minister of State Lau has mentioned that Singaporeans have high expectation of e-services.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Maybe we could look at how Google does it, when they deliver services to all of us, they have Google Beta, Google Preview, using this to communicate to people that some services —

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: — may be a trial, and how can we better communicate the expectations?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Minister Josephine Teo, please, if you could keep your response concise.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Minister of State Jasmin Lau can supplement, but maybe very quickly, on citizen expectations.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We do not see it in a bad way.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Member and I use digital services all the time.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And for us as citizens to want the Government to do better, in terms of digital Government services delivery, is a very natural thing.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And so, we want to hold ourselves to higher standards.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But the Member's point, I think is a very useful one to keep in mind, which is that the expectations around failures, the expectations around what we may need to do to introduce more security that could come at the expense of some convenience that we have been used to, that is something that we need to socialise more people to.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In cybersecurity, we always say that there is a trade-off.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: When things are able to move in a very fast way, you worry about whether the security features have been properly built-in, and there may be times that we need to prioritise the security more than the convenience.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, the same for some of the services that we may have to offer, we do not know for a fact that we need that sort of thing and we will try, not to purposely, to deliberately, introduce inconvenience.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But if and when we need to, we have to explain to people and do so properly.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I do not know whether Minister of State Jasmin Lau wants to add on.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Minister of State Jasmin, you have one minute.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: I mentioned faster and better services just now, but it is very important that we do not view digital transformation as just one or two metrics.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: Our systems must be fast, but also secure.

speaker: The Chairman
text: On that note, Mr Sharael Taha, would you wish to withdraw your amendment, please?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: I was hoping to ask another supplementary question, but I will take your guidance, Mr Chairman.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: It evolves not over decades but over months, if not weeks.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: Yet, amid this ambiguity is where ambiguity and velocity — The Chairman: Mr Sharael Taha.
